title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous page (787). X is a surface and I is a finite set of points. Around each x in I there is a small disc D_x, a punctured disc D_x^*, and a boundary circle S_x. The universal cover of D_x^* induces the universal cover \tilde S_x of S_x, and \tilde S_I is the disjoint union of the \tilde S_x. G is a group of homeomorphisms (of X, or of a neighbourhood germ) preserving I. For u in G, Grothendieck sets up a bijection between two kinds of lift. On one side are lifts of u|D_I^* to the universal cover. On the other are lifts \tilde u_S of u|S_I to \tilde S_I that are isomorphisms of T_I-torsors, with T_I = \prod_{x} \pi_1(S_x) \cong Z^I. This gives (143): \tilde G is the group of pairs (u, \tilde u_S). It is an extension of G by T_I, made into a topological group by the coarsest topology making p_1: \tilde G \to G and q_1: \tilde G \to Aut top(\tilde S_I) continuous.

This page first finishes that definition: Aut top(\tilde S_I) carries the compact-open (compact convergence) topology. It then states a comparison result. When X is a compact orientable differentiable surface, the groups just constructed, i.e. the extensions of G (or its completed variant) by T_I, can be described explicitly. They are inverse images, under the canonical homomorphism G \to \Gamma of (141), of a 'special Teichmüller group' S\Gamma \to \Gamma. Formally, \tilde G \cong G \times_\Gamma S\Gamma.

In modern terms: \Gamma is the mapping class group of X with the points of I marked. S\Gamma is the mapping class group of the surface with I replaced by boundary circles, equivalently with tangential framings at the punctures. S\Gamma is a central extension of \Gamma_{g,I} by Z^I, generated by the boundary Dehn twists (the 'capping' sequence). The page asserts that the 'local' extension built from lifts to the universal covers of punctured discs is the pullback of this global Teichmüller-group extension. A profinite or 'hat' version is apparently intended, as suggested by the hats on S and G. This serves the Longue Marche programme of describing Teichmüller groups with tangential base points, i.e. Galois actions on pro-finite Teichmüller towers with Z^I or \hat Z^I twists at the punctures.
errors: No mathematical error is visible, but the key claim is only asserted. The explicit interpretation is announced, apparently with a remark that it involves difficulties, and the page ends without proof.
Some symbols are ambiguous in the image: hat versus tilde on S_I and G, and Aut top versus Autext. This makes it unclear whether the discrete or the profinite version is meant.

ideas.what: Extension of a homeomorphism group G by T_I = Z^I, given by pairs (homeomorphism, lift to the universal covers of the boundary circles or punctured discs), topologized via the compact-open topology on Aut top(\tilde S_I).
ideas.modern_name: Framed / boundary-twist central extension; homeomorphisms with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in mapping class group theory (Dehn twist / capping exact sequences; e.g. Birman, Harer); tangential base points in Galois-theoretic form: Deligne (1989), Ihara
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, points at infinity with tangential data); this precise construction is unsure

ideas.what: Identification of \tilde G with the pullback G \times_\Gamma S\Gamma of a 'special Teichmüller group' S\Gamma \to \Gamma, with kernel Z^I generated by boundary Dehn twists.
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of a surface with boundary as central Z^n-extension of the punctured-surface mapping class group (capping sequence)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses Teichmüller groups; whether 'groupe de Teichmüller spécial' is named there is unsure

missed.claim: The page ends the manuscript by announcing an explicit interpretation of the extensions of G (possibly the profinite \hat G) by T_I as inverse images of a special Teichmüller extension S\Gamma \to \Gamma. It also notes difficulties, and gives no proof.
missed.quote: comme images inverses de un groupe de Teichmüller spécial S\Gamma \to \Gamma, par l'homomorphisme canonique G \to \Gamma dans (141)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The discrete statement is standard. A topological-group or profinite version, with T_I replaced by \hat Z^I and the compact-open topology, ties into Galois actions on profinite mapping class groups with tangential base points. That setting is now well developed (Nakamura, Ihara, Matsumoto), so the unfinished thread was in effect taken up independently.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the closing page of a construction. It identifies a twist extension of a homeomorphism group with the pullback of the standard boundary-twist central extension of the mapping class group, which is well known. It is historically interesting only as Grothendieck's own local-to-global formulation with an explicit topology.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'i.e. Aut top(\tilde S_I) est muni de la convergence compacte' (the image looks like 'Autop'/'Aut top', consistent with q_1 on the previous page), rather than 'Autext'.
The superscript insertion above 'compacte diff.' is 'une surface': 'Dans le cas où X est une surface compacte diff. orientable'.
Line 5 contains a struck-out phrase and an inserted 'explicite, par'. What follows is probably 'des extensions de \hat G par T_I' (or 'une interprétation ... par T_I').
'avec difficultés' is uncertain; it may be 'avec difficultés' or a word like 'différentielles'.
'un groupe de Teichmüller spécial S\Gamma \to \Gamma' — the target may carry a hat (\hat\Gamma) in the image, matching 'G \to \hat\Gamma'; the transcription is inconsistent on this.
